question: Scale conditioning is learned only on symmetric cells c_x = c_y = 2/s with s in [1,4]. Does a decoder whose cell response is an analytic footprint integral (SC-INR: sinc(w_x c_x/2) sinc(w_y c_y/2)) behave differently from decoders that learn the cell as an input token (LIIF concatenation, LTE cell-to-phase) once the cell leaves the training manifold: asymmetric scales, scales above 4, downscaling and cross-scale consistency?
identifiability_argument: With c_x = c_y at every training sample, a first-layer or phase-layer weight pair (w_x, w_y) is constrained only through w_x + w_y. The per-axis response of LIIF and LTE to an asymmetric cell is therefore not determined by training and is expected to vary with the initialisation seed. SC-INR fixes the per-axis response analytically; its frequency map does not depend on the cell.
status: prospective inference on existing checkpoints; no training; one integrated freeze -> run -> score pipeline
seeds_policy: all of seeds 1,2,3 whose checkpoints exist for every model at freeze time; recorded in input_manifest.json

preprocessing.hr_crop: whole image, top-left modcrop to multiples of 24 (lcm of 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 denominators); identical HR support for every condition
preprocessing.lr: torch interpolate bicubic antialias=True align_corners=False to (H/s_y, W/s_x), clamp [0,1]
preprocessing.output: 0.5*network_output+0.5, float32; PSNR-Y uses the clipped output, spectral energies the unclipped output
preprocessing.psnr_y: ITU-R BT.601 luma of clipped RGB, shave ceil(max(s_y, s_x)) pixels, per-image dB
preprocessing.mse_rgb: unclipped RGB mean squared error after a four-pixel shave
preprocessing.spectral: rectangular FFT of the shaved error and target; DC stored separately; energies normalised so that their sum equals the spatial mean square

conditions.asymmetric_in_support: pairs with both scales <= 4 (eight pairs); pairs containing 6 are reported separately

cell_policies.native: decoder cell (2/s_y, 2/s_x): the true per-axis footprint
cell_policies.swap: decoder cell (2/s_x, 2/s_y): axes exchanged; wrong on both axes, same multiset of values
cell_policies.iso: decoder cell (2/g, 2/g) with g = sqrt(s_y s_x): a symmetric substitute inside the training manifold

conditions.consistency_metric: from one LR (HR/s_hi), predict the full grid at s_hi and the half grid at s_lo = s_hi/2; compare the 2x2 box average of the s_hi output with the s_lo output (RGB PSNR, shave 4 on the low grid); also compare both with the box-averaged HR and the bicubic-antialiased HR

downscale.input: centre crop of the HR image with the given side, fed as the network input
references: bicubic antialiased resize of the input

conditions.u_bins: u = 2 s r with Chebyshev radius r; width 0.25 up to u = 4 plus an overflow bin; asymmetric conditions use u = max(2 s_y |f_y|, 2 s_x |f_x|) and additionally a 5x5 grid over (u_y, u_x) with edges 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, inf

scoring.balanced_mean: per image -> per dataset -> equal weight over datasets -> equal weight over the conditions named by each statistic; seeds averaged per image before any contrast
scoring.bootstrap: paired image bootstrap within each dataset, 10,000 resamples, numpy default_rng(20261101); one index draw per dataset shared by all statistics; intervals condition on the trained seeds
scoring.gate_alpha: one-sided 0.05/5 lower bounds for the five registered gates; descriptive statistics use two-sided 95% intervals

predictions_frozen_before_run.G1_scinr_axis_identified: SC-INR, eight in-support asymmetric pairs: balanced mean of PSNR-Y(native) - PSNR-Y(swap) has corrected lower bound > 0, and every seed's balanced mean is > 0.
predictions_frozen_before_run.G2a_scinr_exceeds_liif: The native-minus-swap gain of SC-INR exceeds that of LIIF: corrected lower bound of the paired difference-of-differences > 0.
predictions_frozen_before_run.G3_scinr_native_beats_iso: SC-INR: PSNR-Y(native) - PSNR-Y(iso) over the eight in-support pairs has corrected lower bound > 0.
predictions_frozen_before_run.G4_consistency: Prior uncertain (the sinc weights precede a nonlinear MLP and the bilinear skip ignores the footprint). SC-INR's consistency PSNR, averaged over the two pairs, exceeds both LIIF's and LTE's with corrected lower bounds > 0.
descriptive_not_gated: LIIF and LTE native-minus-swap and native-minus-iso per seed with two-sided intervals: the identifiability argument predicts seed-dependent signs and native <= iso.
Asymmetric degradation relative to the symmetric references at s_y and s_x for every model.
R(u_y, u_x) grids per model and policy: a wrong cell on one axis should raise error along that axis for SC-INR only.
Pairs containing 6, scales 6/8/12 and the downscale condition: PSNR and R profiles, expected to be dominated by the shared encoder with small decoder differences.

interpretations.A_footprint: If G1-G3 pass and LIIF/LTE show seed-dependent or non-positive native-minus-iso gains, the analytic footprint response is what makes the cell well defined outside the training manifold; the symmetric in-support equality of all decoders (stage 02) is then the first prediction of the same account.
interpretations.B_token: If LIIF and LTE match SC-INR's native-minus-swap gain, the learned token generalises per axis without having been trained on asymmetric cells and the identifiability argument is wrong in practice; if G4 fails while G1-G3 pass, the current SC-INR is footprint-aware in its features but not footprint-exact in its output, which motivates a linear-readout variant.

decision_rule: Report all outcomes. Only if A is supported does the planned next stage (an exact linear-readout variant and the never-trained no-sinc ablation) justify training time.
compute: GPU inference only on devices named at launch; about 40 full-image forward passes per image and checkpoint; no training runs.
